display.purpose: The name on the home page only, stacked one word per line at up to 10rem, widened on Archivo's wdth axis. The second line steps down in weight rather than in grey.

headline.purpose: The page title on every page except the home page.

title.purpose: Section headings, separated by space rather than by a rule.

lede.purpose: The single sentence under a title, in Secondary Ink at a 56ch cap. On the home page it opens with the affiliation.

label.purpose: Monospace for pin captions, breadcrumbs, card tags, meta lines, chart text, table headers and the footer. Never prose.

figure.purpose: Monospace with tabular lining numerals for any number that will be compared against another number.

shadows.name: pin-rest
shadows.purpose: The board pin at rest: a contact shadow plus a wide, heavily negative-spread ambient. The only shadow in the system.

shadows.name: pin-lift
shadows.purpose: The same two layers grown, paired with a 6px rise, on pin hover and focus-visible.

motion.name: ease-rise
motion.purpose: The one easing curve on the site, used for every lift and for the preview shelf entry.

motion.name: duration-button
motion.purpose: Button transform. Colour changes on the same element run at 0.2s.

motion.name: duration-card
motion.purpose: Card transform and border-colour, and the preview shelf entry animation.

motion.name: duration-pin
motion.purpose: Board pin transform, box-shadow and border-colour.

motion.name: lift-button
motion.purpose: Hover rise for a pill action.

motion.name: lift-card
motion.purpose: Hover rise for a project card.

motion.name: lift-pin
motion.purpose: Hover and focus-visible rise for a board pin, gated behind (hover: hover) and prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: reduced-motion-kill
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation: none !important; transition-duration: .01ms !important; } html { scroll-behavior: auto; } }
motion.purpose: The global revocation. Animated image formats are not covered by it, which is why the board ships stills and upgrades in JavaScript.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one ink-filled pill action per viewport. The rise is the whole hover feedback; the fill does not change.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-block; text-decoration: none; border-radius: var(--pill); padding: .72rem 1.4rem; font-family: var(--body); font-size: .92rem; font-weight: 550; letter-spacing: -0.01em; border: 1px solid var(--line); color: var(--ink); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 75%, transparent); transition: transform .28s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), background-color .2s, border-color .2s; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); border-color: var(--ink); } .ds-btn:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A translucent white pill over the field. Goes fully opaque and steps its border up to Secondary Ink on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-block; text-decoration: none; border-radius: var(--pill); padding: .72rem 1.4rem; font-family: var(--body); font-size: .92rem; font-weight: 550; letter-spacing: -0.01em; border: 1px solid var(--line); color: var(--ink); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 75%, transparent); transition: transform .28s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), background-color .2s, border-color .2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); border-color: var(--dim); background: var(--surface); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Board Pin
components.description: The signature component: a whole real artifact as a link, with a two-line face underneath. Ships a still and carries its animation in data-motion.
components.html: A convolutional agent playing Flappy Bird from rendered framesafter-hours
components.css: .ds-pin { max-width: 320px; } .ds-pin > a { display: block; position: relative; text-decoration: none; color: inherit; border-radius: var(--r); overflow: hidden; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px #1010140A, 0 10px 26px -18px #10101433; transition: transform .34s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), box-shadow .34s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), border-color .34s; } .ds-pin img { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; background: var(--sunken); } .ds-pin-face { display: block; padding: .85rem .95rem 1rem; } .ds-pin-what { display: block; font-family: var(--body); font-size: .9rem; font-weight: 550; letter-spacing: -0.015em; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--ink); } .ds-pin-where { display: block; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: .72rem; color: var(--muted); margin-top: .35rem; } @media (hover: hover) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-pin > a:hover, .ds-pin > a:focus-visible { transform: translateY(-6px); box-shadow: 0 2px 6px #1010140F, 0 26px 50px -24px #1010143D; } } .ds-pin > a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Project Card
components.description: A link card with a monospace tag, a title and a description. Can drive the preview panel through a data-preview key.
components.html: workafter-hoursFlappy Bird from raw pixels, sorting rendered, 3-SAT over GF(2).
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--r); padding: 1.1rem 1.2rem; display: block; max-width: 320px; text-decoration: none; color: var(--ink); font-family: var(--body); transition: transform .3s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), border-color .3s; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: var(--dim); } .ds-card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-card-tag { display: block; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: .72rem; color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: .5rem; } .ds-card-title { display: block; font-weight: 620; letter-spacing: -0.02em; margin-bottom: .25rem; } .ds-card-desc { display: block; color: var(--dim); font-size: .91rem; line-height: 1.55; }

components.name: Hero Pane
components.description: The opening surface: translucent over the field rather than a solid card, so the one piece of colour the site owns shows through. Nothing sits above the name.
components.html:
MohamedHamlil

M1 Artificial Intelligence at Université Grenoble Alpes, with research internships in computer algebra and in industrial economics.
components.css: .ds-hero { padding: clamp(2.4rem, 6vw, 4.5rem) clamp(1.4rem, 4vw, 3rem) clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3rem); text-align: center; border-radius: var(--r); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 44%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(22px) saturate(1.2); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(22px) saturate(1.2); border: 1px solid var(--line); } .ds-hero-name { margin: 0 0 clamp(1.2rem, 2.5vw, 1.8rem); font-family: var(--display); font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 9vw, 5rem); font-weight: 800; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 118; letter-spacing: -0.05em; line-height: .88; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink); text-wrap: balance; } .ds-line { display: block; } .ds-line-dim { font-weight: 500; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 112; } .ds-lede { font-family: var(--body); color: var(--dim); font-size: clamp(1rem, 1.2vw, 1.1rem); line-height: 1.55; max-width: 56ch; margin: 0 auto; }

components.name: Site Header
components.description: Sticky, translucent over the ground, 58px tall. Monospace breadcrumbs and a pill repository link; the wordmark is the only non-mono item.
components.html: Mohamed HamlilHomeGitHub
components.css: .ds-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; min-height: 58px; flex-wrap: wrap; padding: 0 clamp(18px, 3.5vw, 40px); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--paper) 70%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.2); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); font-family: var(--body); } .ds-head a { text-decoration: none; } .ds-brand { font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.03em; color: var(--ink); font-variation-settings: "wdth" 110; } .ds-crumbs, .ds-crumbs a { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: .78rem; color: var(--dim); } .ds-crumbs a:hover { color: var(--ink); } .ds-spacer { flex: 1; } .ds-repo { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: .78rem; color: var(--ink); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--pill); padding: .4rem .9rem; transition: border-color .2s, background-color .2s; } .ds-repo:hover { border-color: var(--dim); background: var(--surface); } .ds-repo:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Preview Panel
components.description: A sticky panel that fills with what is inside whatever is pointed at or focused. Figures are contained on their own ground, never cropped. At rest it sits at half strength.
components.html: Point at anything below to see what is inside it.
components.css: .ds-preview { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--r); padding: .85rem; max-width: 520px; } .ds-pv-frame { min-height: 152px; display: grid; place-items: center; } .ds-pv-shelf { display: grid; grid-auto-flow: column; grid-auto-columns: 1fr; gap: .6rem; width: 100%; animation: ds-pv-in .3s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1); } .ds-pv-shelf img { width: 100%; height: 152px; object-fit: contain; object-position: center; border-radius: var(--r-sm); background: var(--raised); display: block; border: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 4px; } @keyframes ds-pv-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } } .ds-preview[data-state="rest"] .ds-pv-shelf img { opacity: .5; filter: saturate(.5); } .ds-preview[data-state="rest"] .ds-pv-cap { opacity: .75; } .ds-pv-cap { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: .74rem; color: var(--muted); margin: .7rem .15rem 0; line-height: 1.5; } @media (max-width: 640px) { .ds-pv-shelf { grid-auto-flow: row; grid-auto-columns: auto; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); } .ds-pv-shelf img { height: 104px; } }

narrative.overview:
Twelve real captures are pinned to a light wall under a single soft light. The site owns exactly one piece of colour, an iridescent field fixed behind the page, and it spends it entirely on the first viewport before fading out above the work. Everything below that is white, ink and hairlines, because ten of the twelve pins are figures rendered on white by four repositories this site does not build. A surface that matches them is what stops the page fighting its own content.

The density is Pinterest, not portfolio: a four-column masonry board of unequal tiles begins immediately under the opening pane, with no section heading, no teaser copy and no table of contents between the name and the work. Chrome is deliberately thin, a 58px sticky bar and a mono footer, and it recedes rather than frames. The name is the only display-scale element on the site, set in Archivo at up to 10rem, widened on its wdth axis and stacked one word per line. Monospace appears only where the content is machine truth: captions, paths, table headers, chart labels and figures.

The confirmed rejections are structural. Nothing sits above a heading, so there are no kickers or eyebrow labels anywhere in the build. There is no dark scheme, by decision rather than omission. And no component is allowed to be colourful on its own account: an accent hue exists for exactly one purpose, marking a published correction.
keyCharacteristics: One iridescent field, masked out before the board; every component is white, ink and hairline.
A four-column masonry board of real artifacts, animated pins sorted to the front.
Hairlines and translucency instead of shadows, with a two-step shadow reserved for one component.
Archivo at two axes: one family carries both the display name and the body text.
Monospace strictly for labels, paths, captions and figures, never for prose.
Light only, permanently, with a stated precondition for reconsidering it.

rules.name: The Field-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour lives in the fixed field behind the page and nowhere else. The field is masked to transparent before the board begins, so no pin is ever read against a gradient. Components are white, ink and hairline; if a surface needs to feel coloured, it becomes translucent and lets the field through instead of tinting itself.

rules.name: The Correction Rule
rules.body: Correction Rust marks a published correction and nothing else. It never becomes a link colour, a hover state, a brand accent or a chart series.

rules.name: The No Dark Scheme Rule
rules.body: There is deliberately no dark scheme, and color-scheme: light is declared so the browser cannot theme form controls and scrollbars for a page the site never renders. Ten of the twelve board figures are rendered on white by repositories this site does not build; inverting around them produces twelve white slabs on black, which is the exact failure the light world was chosen to avoid. A dark scheme becomes possible the day those figures are re-rendered on dark grounds, and not before.

rules.name: The Shared Names Rule
rules.body: public/site/tokens.css is served unhashed at a stable URL and linked across the origin by sibling sites. Its custom-property names are an additive-only contract pinned in site/tokens.lock.json: values may change freely and names may be added, but removing or renaming one has to happen in the same commit as the lock file. The file holds custom properties only; anything with a selector belongs in a site stylesheet where the bundler can hash it.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-For-Evidence Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks machine truth: a path, a file name, a label, a caption, a figure, a table header. It never sets prose, a heading, a button or a lede. If a monospace run is a sentence the reader is meant to read for meaning, it is in the wrong face.

rules.name: The One Family, Two Axes Rule
rules.body: Display and body are the same Archivo stack. Hierarchy comes from weight, the wdth axis and scale, never from introducing a second sans. A new display face is a change to the world, not a styling choice.

rules.name: The Metric Fallback Rule
rules.body: The name is set at up to 160px, so the swap from a fallback face is the most visible moment on a cold cache. Archivo Metric is a local-only @font-face (Arial, Helvetica Neue, Liberation Sans) with size-adjust: 97%, ascent-override: 90% and descent-override: 22%, so the first paint is the same size and shape as the loaded face. Any new face that carries the name inherits this obligation.

rules.name: The Nothing Above A Heading Rule
rules.body: No kicker, eyebrow, or category label sits above a heading anywhere on the site. Information that wants that position goes into the first sentence beneath the name instead. This is a divergence from the build's own FIRST VIEWPORT line, which specified a mono course label above the name; the label was deleted in the finish review and the affiliation now opens the lede. There is no .chip rule in the stylesheet and no chip in the markup: the code is the record.

rules.name: The Work Starts Immediately Rule
rules.body: The board begins directly under the opening pane, with no section heading and no intervening copy. Nothing may be inserted between the first viewport and the first artifact.

rules.name: The Motion-First Fill Rule
rules.body: Pins are flattened across all projects and sorted so that animated ones lead, rather than being grouped by project. A column-filled masonry lays out column by column, so grouping by project buries three of the four loops at the bottom of a column the first screen never reaches. Known trade-off: this puts the three heaviest images in column one, so the board reads left-loud. Weighed and accepted; leading with motion won over even visual weight.

rules.name: The Hairline-First Rule
rules.body: A new surface separates itself with a 1px hairline and, if it sits over the field, with translucency. It does not reach for a shadow. Shadows on this site are a property of the board pin, not a global elevation scale.

rules.name: The Lift Ladder Rule
rules.body: Rise on hover scales with the size of the thing lifted: a button rises 2px, a card 4px, a pin 6px. All three use the same cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) ease over 0.28s to 0.34s. A larger lift on a smaller element reads as a glitch.

rules.name: The Two Radii and a Pill Rule
rules.body: 20px for surfaces, 12px for figures nested inside a surface, 999px for actions. A new radius value is a new shape language and needs a reason.

rules.name: The Stills-First Rule
rules.body: The markup ships the still and carries the animation in data-motion; the entry script swaps the source only when prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference matches. Shipping it the other way meant an animated WebP that kept looping under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, because no CSS rule stops an animated image playing. Two consequences are accepted honestly: with JavaScript off the board is twelve stills rather than twelve moving things, and each of the four motion pins fetches twice, the still and then the animation.

rules.name: The Alt-Empty Pin Rule
rules.body: A pin image carries alt="" because the description it would announce is the visible caption immediately below it, inside the same link. Repeating it would make a screen reader say the whole pin twice. This rule holds only while the caption lives inside the link; a decorative-only pin without a caption would need real alt text.

dos: Do put every new surface on white (#FFFFFF) with a 1px hairline (#1010141F) and a 20px radius, on the #F7F7F9 ground.
Do let a surface that sits over the field be translucent with a backdrop blur rather than tinted, so the field shows through instead of being covered.
Do reserve monospace for labels, paths, captions, table headers and figures, and set every number that will be compared with tabular-nums lining.
Do scale hover rise with element size: 2px for a button, 4px for a card, 6px for a pin, all on cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1).
Do gate motion behind both (hover: hover) and prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, and handle animated image formats in JavaScript, because no CSS rule stops an animated image looping.
Do give focus everything hover has: :focus-visible shares every hover rule on the pin, and focus drives the preview panel exactly as the pointer does.
Do add token names to public/site/tokens.css freely, and change values freely, but treat removal or renaming as a contract break that must land in the same commit as site/tokens.lock.json.
Do keep the shared token file selector-free; anything with a selector belongs in a site stylesheet the bundler can hash.
donts: Don't put a kicker, eyebrow, or category label above a heading. Put that information in the first sentence beneath it.
Don't add a dark scheme until the board's figures are re-rendered on dark grounds. Inverting the page around figures drawn on white is the failure this world was chosen to avoid.
Don't give a component a colour of its own. Colour is the field's, and the field stops above the board.
Don't use Correction Rust (#B23A1B) for anything but a published correction, and never as a link, hover, brand or chart colour.
Don't reach for --teal or --gold; they exist only so four sibling project sites can migrate one at a time.
Don't add a shadow to a new component. Hairline plus translucency is the depth model; the two-step shadow belongs to the board pin.
Don't introduce a second sans-serif or a display-only face. Hierarchy comes from Archivo's weight and wdth axes.
Don't set prose, headings, buttons or ledes in monospace.
Don't crop a figure to fill a frame. Charts are contained on their own ground, never covered, because cropping a result turns it into wallpaper.
Don't load anything from a CDN or let third-party code run in the browser; charts are hand-drawn SVG and every dependency is bundled from source.
